column1: # The raw log is the forensic record of a flight: every line received, corrupted ones
# included, written as "<receipt time> TAB <escaped payload>". A corrupted payload can
# contain any byte, so tab, CR, LF and backslash become two-character escapes and every
# other control character becomes \xNN — that is what keeps one record on one line.
# Two implementations undo it, and they must agree exactly:
# They did not. The web console stripped the timestamp and replayed the payload still
# escaped, so exactly the records a forensic replay exists to inspect came back as
# something the vehicle never sent. This file is why that cannot happen again.
# Format: <id> TAB <escaped> TAB <plain, as lower-case UTF-8 hex>
# The plain text is hex because it is allowed to contain tabs and newlines — a fixture
# file cannot carry it literally, which is the same reason the log escapes it.
